The answer for who curious of Vietnamese cuisine (Not Pho, not Nem). Super comfortable food
Mar 2018 • Friends
First, this is absolutely not a fast food restaurant. It has been just lovely to find such a place for a foodie spirit like me.
1/ Clean food: The food is freshly made everyday, plenty of green and veggies, culture food.., kinda Mama cooking style... so comfortable like a hug. must try: Frogs noodle, Bun Bo Hue, Hen Xao... Set lunch is splendid. 
2/ Welcome atmosphere, sweet service: people are lovely there, I go there during my time in Saigon for lunch, almost everyday. As Anh - the owner is a professional in hospitality business, He and his team always address the client's need in a very professional but heart warming manners.
3/ Great value for money: less than 3 USD for a complete set lunch (rice, veggies, veggies soup, meat or fish, tea) deal could not be better than this.
4/ Location: pretty central, district one, 10 mins driving from the notre dame cathedral (Nha tho Duc Ba). 
what else??? i don't know what to say anyway, because I just in love with this place... I will be back for sure.

They decide what you eat, not you!
Jul 2017 • Solo
The food is not bad, but the problem is that when you go there you order one thing and they serve yousomething different without even informing you or apologising... I went there specifically to have the frog noodles, the guy who seems to be the manager and speaks quite good english tried to convince me to have the pork noodles but I said I wanted the frog noodles. When the food came to the table they simply served me pork noodles. When I asked the manager if that was frog he said that it was pork, when I said that I had asked for frog he just said that the pork is very good and very famous, he did not apologise, did not explain why I was served pork when I ordered frog, nothing. He just seems that he doesn't care what you order, he just serves you what he thinks you should eat and seems to find it very natural and normal, without even apologising or explaining anything. It's just like that because he wants to and decides for you... Quite bad experience! I don't like other people to decide what I should eat or not, if I want an opinion or suggestion I will ask for one, but if I order something specific and if thw waiter says yes I expect to have what I order. As simple as that!

One of the best restaurants in Ho Chi Minh City!
Mar 2017 • Couples
This restaurant is owned by Tran Anh and his wife, Ha. Both of them are delightful hosts and more important, ambassadors of promoting the food of Hue (a region in Vietnam). 

These are the dishes you should absolutely experience if you go to this restaurant:

1. Bun Bo Hue (called simply Bun Bo locally), which features round rice noodles, as opposed to pho’s flat ones, mixed into a stock made from beef and/or pork bones, flavored with lemongrass, annatto seeds, ginger, fermented shrimp paste, sugar and chiles.

and, 

2. Banh Beo . . . These are steamed rice cakes, about the size of a silver dollar, that come five pieces to an order, topped with dried shrimp, pork cracklings, shallots and herbs and served with nuoc mam pha. They’re cooked in one of two vessels which determine their full name and shape: Banh beo chen are steamed and served in small ceramic saucers (chen) while Banh beo dia are cooked in a slightly larger metal form that resembles a hard-boiled egg platter, and served on a larger plate.

The atmosphere of this restaurant is very comfortable and stylish. Anh and Ha have done an excellent job in designing this restaurant. The dishes prepared by the kitchen staff are made with fresh ingredients. The prices are quite reasonable. By the way, Anh went to university in Europe and is quite comfortable speaking English. Additionally, he was the former manager of the Liberty Hotel Greenview before him and his wife started this restaurant. I would unequivocally recommend this restaurant. You wont be disappointed!
